# Cathra

> Cathra (cathra.dev) is a free research and education tool that uses machine learning to compare an ovarian ultrasound image to two learned patterns, normal and abnormal ovarian appearance, and returns a similarity score for each. It runs entirely in the web browser, so images are never uploaded. It is not a medical device and does not diagnose any condition.

Key facts:

- Name: Cathra (also written "Cathra AI" or "cathra.dev"). Not related to "Catra", the She-Ra character.
- Website: https://www.cathra.dev
- Built by: Teddy Aaron, a high school founder from Greenwich, Connecticut.
- Owner: Teddy Aaron Ventures LLC.
- Price: free. No accounts, no cookies, no image uploads.
- Model: a neural network (model v2) trained on 1,734 images from the public PCOSGen ovarian ultrasound dataset (Handa et al., 2025, CC BY 4.0) and tested on 1,449 held-out images: 85.6% accuracy and 81.1% balanced accuracy. These are research results on one public dataset, not clinical performance.
- Answer rule: Cathra names a pattern only when the scores clear thresholds calibrated with conformal prediction (normal at 60% or higher, abnormal at about 97% or higher). Otherwise it shows "Unable to assess confidently."
- PCOS: most abnormal images in the training data show a polycystic ovarian appearance, but Cathra does not detect or diagnose PCOS or any other condition.
- Paper: Aaron, T. (2026). Cathra: An In-Browser Classifier for Normal and Abnormal Ovarian Ultrasound Appearance [Preprint]. Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24118082
- Intended use: research and education only. Ultrasound images should be interpreted by a qualified medical professional.

## Tools

- [Analyze an ovarian ultrasound image](https://www.cathra.dev/analyze): choose a JPG or PNG ovarian ultrasound image and get normal and abnormal pattern similarity scores, computed on the user's device.
- [Cathra Dataset Check](https://www.cathra.dev/dataset-check): free in-browser tool that finds exact copies, near-copies, images with conflicting labels, and train/test leaks in a folder of medical images. Nothing is uploaded.

## Docs

- [How Cathra works](https://www.cathra.dev/how-it-works): training data, v1 vs v2 test results, how to read the scores, the calibrated answer rule, FAQ, and limitations.
- [Cathra research and teaching](https://www.cathra.dev/research): the preprint and abstract, how to cite Cathra, a 30-minute classroom lesson, and the changelog.
- [Privacy and terms](https://www.cathra.dev/privacy): images never leave the device; medical and legal disclaimer; ownership.
- [Founder: Teddy Aaron](https://www.cathra.dev/founder): who built Cathra and why.

## Learn

- [What does a normal ovary look like on ultrasound?](https://www.cathra.dev/learn/normal-ovary-ultrasound): Shape, follicles, and how a normal ovary changes across the cycle.
- [What does a polycystic ovary look like on ultrasound?](https://www.cathra.dev/learn/polycystic-ovary-ultrasound): Many small follicles, the guideline thresholds, and why it isn’t the same as PCOS.
- [How accurate is AI at reading ultrasounds?](https://www.cathra.dev/learn/ai-ultrasound-accuracy): Why one accuracy number can mislead, and what to ask about any AI tool.
- [Can AI detect PCOS from an ultrasound?](https://www.cathra.dev/learn/can-ai-detect-pcos): An honest answer: what ultrasound AI can and can’t tell you about PCOS.
- [Why duplicate images make medical AI look better than it is](https://www.cathra.dev/learn/duplicate-images-medical-ai): How copied and mislabeled images inflate results, with a real dataset example.

## Optional

- [Full text of every page](https://www.cathra.dev/llms-full.txt): all of the above in one plain-text file.
- [Paper (PDF)](https://www.cathra.dev/cathra-paper.pdf): the full preprint.
- [Hemra](https://hemraresarch.teddyaaron.com): sister project by the same founder that compares white blood cell images to learned cell types in the browser.
